negative_action: Relying solely on written materials or outdated guidelines
description: Do not depend only on textbooks or outdated standards instead of current physician or expert guidance.
risk: Therapeutic interventions may not meet current best practices, increasing risk of harm or ineffective treatment.

description: Do not reproduce copyrighted materials beyond allowed limits.
risk: Legal issues and professional misconduct allegations.

description: Do not neglect to set a session agenda or structure sessions poorly.
risk: Sessions may become unfocused, reducing therapeutic effectiveness.

description: Do not breach patient confidentiality, especially in sharing case material.
risk: Loss of patient trust and ethical violations.

description: Do not neglect your own self-care or ignore burnout.
risk: Burnout can lead to decreased therapy quality and therapist well-being.

description: Do not communicate in a top-down or authoritarian manner.
risk: Reduces patient engagement and inhibits therapeutic alliance.

negative_action: Glossing over genuine problems or distress
description: Do not minimize or dismiss significant patient emotions or circumstances.
risk: Patient may feel invalidated or unheard, hampering progress.

description: Do not use excessive empathy, warmth, or humor during sessions.
risk: May unintentionally reinforce negative cognitions or backfire.

negative_action: Colluding with maladaptive thoughts or behaviors
description: Do not passively validate or reinforce maladaptive patterns.
risk: Entrenches unhelpful cognitions or behaviors.

description: Do not use monolithic or inflexible therapeutic styles.
risk: Fails to address unique patient needs and reduces efficacy.

negative_action: Labeling patients in a pejorative way
description: Do not use diagnostic terms to distance or insult patients.
risk: Harms the therapeutic relationship and increases stigma.

description: Do not accede to inappropriate requests for friendship, intimacy, or favors.
risk: Blurs professional boundaries, leading to ethical violations.

negative_action: Proceeding with CBT in presence of absolute contraindications
description: Do not use CBT when patients have absolute contraindications (e.g., advanced dementia, severe antisocial traits).
risk: Likely to result in poor outcomes or even harm.

description: Do not minimize, overlook, or neglect to address suicidality, hopelessness, or associated risks.
risk: Potential for increased suicide risk and patient harm.

description: Do not skip assessment of model compatibility or patient rationale.
risk: May cause disengagement or resistance to treatment.

description: Do not use unchanging conceptualizations—revise as new info emerges.
risk: Overlooks evolving patient needs; may miss important treatment targets.

description: Do not skip symptom measurements and standardized progress tracking.
risk: May miss signs of deterioration or lack of improvement.

negative_action: Using vague, non-specific, or overwhelming goals
description: Do not set overly vague or unrealistic goals or agenda items.
risk: Patients may feel overwhelmed or lost and progress is hindered.

negative_action: Giving overly positive or critical feedback
description: Do not provide feedback that is exaggerated (either positive or negative).
risk: May reinforce denial or decrease motivation.

negative_action: Ignoring patient education level or therapy history
description: Do not neglect to tailor psychoeducation to patient’s background.
risk: Patient may misunderstand or disengage from therapy.

negative_action: Inappropriately using role play with unstable patients
description: Do not use role play with patients lacking reality testing or with severe personality/psychotic disorders unless highly experienced.
risk: May destabilize patients or worsen symptoms.

negative_action: Pushing for cognitive error labeling if discouraging
description: Do not force patients to label or distinguish cognitive errors if it causes confusion.
risk: Risk of discouragement or disengagement.

negative_action: Overwhelming with complex tasks early in therapy
description: Do not overload new patients with complicated record-keeping or analyses.
risk: Patient may feel overwhelmed and give up.

negative_action: Using leading, closed, or overly challenging Socratic questions
description: Do not frame Socratic inquiry in ways that make the therapist the only expert.
risk: Patients may feel judged or less autonomous.

description: Do not promote ungrounded positive alternatives, especially after trauma or severe loss.
risk: Patient may feel invalidated or misunderstood.

negative_action: Proceeding with advanced interventions before readiness
description: Do not attempt complex interventions before basic skills are established.
risk: Patient may not benefit or may disengage from therapy.

negative_action: Assigning tasks that are too ambitious or mismatched
description: Do not assign tasks beyond the patient’s current capacity.
risk: Patients may feel overwhelmed and unsuccessful.

description: Do not assign solutions or tasks without patient collaboration.
risk: Reduces patient buy-in and willingness.

negative_action: Criticizing or blaming patients for noncompletion
description: Do not blame or label the patient for failing homework.
risk: Damages alliance and reduces motivation.

description: Do not give the patient an excessive or complicated list of homework.
risk: Leads to cognitive overload and potential dropout.

description: Do not reinforce safety or avoidance behaviors, directly or indirectly.
risk: Maintains or worsens the issue the therapy is aiming to treat.

negative_action: Pushing exposure/homework at an inappropriate pace
description: Do not push assignments that are too easy, too hard, or poorly timed.
risk: Can cause excessive anxiety or lack of progress.

description: Do not prescribe exposure or response prevention in an authoritarian manner.
risk: Undermines trust and reduces efficacy.

description: Do not challenge core beliefs before building alliance or ensuring readiness.
risk: Patient may become defensive or drop out.

description: Do not pursue schema work without supporting understanding and safety.
risk: May evoke distress or confusion.

negative_action: Challenging hopelessness or suicidality before alliance
description: Do not directly confront these core issues without a secure therapeutic relationship.
risk: Patient may feel invalidated, defensive, or experience increased risk.

description: Do not proceed with imaginal or distressing interventions without preparation and explicit patient agreement.
risk: Traumatization or violation of trust.

negative_action: Neglecting safety and confidentiality with high-risk patients
description: Do not overlook the specifics of confidentiality or safety planning.
risk: Patient or others may be put at increased risk.

description: Do not proceed when acute medical or psychiatric instability is present.
risk: Could worsen patient condition or miss critical medical needs.

description: Do not overlook major comorbidities in planning and delivering CBT.
risk: Poor outcomes and risk of exacerbation.

negative_action: Rigidly applying session format with impaired patients
description: Do not demand standard format when a patient’s participation is compromised.
risk: Increases disengagement and could worsen symptoms.

negative_action: Continuing treatment when patient is intoxicated
description: Do not proceed with sessions if patient is intoxicated or sobriety is violated.
risk: Therapy is unlikely to be productive and could be unsafe.

negative_action: Exceeding reasonable workload or neglecting self-care
description: Do not overload yourself or allow work-life imbalance.
risk: Risks burnout, lower performance, and suboptimal care.

description: Do not treat cases beyond your expertise; refer out when needed.
risk: Patient safety and outcomes may be compromised.

negative_action: Ignoring evidence or prematurely forming conclusions
description: Do not ignore counter-evidence or overgeneralize from limited data.
risk: Can lead to faulty conceptualizations and poor intervention choices.

description: Do not overlook the need for safety plans with high-risk patients.
risk: Increases likelihood of patient harm.
